caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 525 of 2000
lawyer:
Md Nowab Ali, Advocate-on-Record --For the Petitioners 	
Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record -For Respondent No. 1 
Not represented -Respondent Nos. 2-10.
parties:
Kartic Chandra Sarker being dead his heirs Samiran Sarker and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Anarathi Mondal and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 19-1-2000 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 449 of 1992).
full_judgment:
Syed JR Mudassir Husain J: The petitioners, the substituted heirs of original defendant N6. 1 Kartic Chandra Sarker, are seeking leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 19-1-2000 passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute in Civil Revision No. 449 of 1992.

2. The plaintiff-respondent No. 1 Srimati Anarathi Mondal instituted Title Suit No. 73 of 1983 on 2-3-1983 in the Court of Munsif now Assistant Judge, Khulna against the said defendant No. 1 and others praying for a declaration that the compromise decree dated 21-6-1962 passed in the earlier Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 of the 1st Court of Munsif, Khulna filed by the said defendant No. 1 against the respondent No. 1 is forged, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon her (respondent No. 1) stating to the effect that the suit land belonged to her father Bisturam Gain and RS and SA Khatian were correctly recorded in her father's name; that the said defendant No. 1 Kartic Chandra Sarker was a village quack and a litigant person of the locality. The plaintiffs father died leaving behind her as only daughter and 3 grandsons to inherit properties left by said Bishuram; that plaintiff possessed the suit land on payment of rent. But when the plaintiffs son Bimal went to pay rent in the year 1983 he was surprised to see the name of Kartic Chandra Sarker defendant No. 1 in the record of right in place of her father Bisturam Gain; that on an inquiry it was detected that said defendant No.1 mutated his name in Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1978-79 on the basis of a compromise decree dated 21-6-1962 passed in Title Suit No. 182 of 1962. Against the present respondent No. 1; that plaintiff respondent never received any summons or notice as defendant and she did not compromise the suit by putting her thumb impression in any application of compromise. The alleged compromise decree was obtained by practicing fraud. The defendant No. 1 contested the instant suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations contending, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to Bisturam Gain, father of the respondent No. 1. But said Bisturam settled the suit land orally to him (defendant No. 1) and subsequently, granted an 'Amalnama' in Jaistha 1356 BS; that Bisturam also granted him rent receipt and delivered possession of the suit land. During SA operation the name of Bisturam was wrongly recorded in the SA Khatian and the plaintiff respondent as daughter of Bisturam was claiming the suit land and, as such, the said defendant No. 1 (predecessor of leave-petitioners) had to file Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 and that suit was compromised between the respondent No. 1 and the defendant No. 1 (predecessor of the present petitioners). The compromise was genuine and defendant No. 1 has been in possession of the suit land for long over 12 years and thereby acquired a valid title in the suit land.

3. The learned Munsif by his judgment and decree dated 14-12-1988 decreed the suit in favour of the respondent No. 1 and against which the defendant No. 1 (the predecessor of the present leave-petitioners) filed Title Appeal No. 26 of 1989 and the appellate Court allowed the same by dismissing the suit. The plaintiff respondent then moved the High Court Division in revision and the Rule obtained was made absolute by the impugned judgment of the High Court Division.

4. Mr. Nowab Ali; the learned Advocate-on-Record, placed before us the judgments of the courts below and then submitted that the learned Single Judge misread and misdirected himself in not adverting to definite finding of the appellate Court to the effect that the 'Left Thumb Impression' (LTI) of the plaintiff, appearing on the petition of compromise filed along with two other defendants, in the previous Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 of defendant was endorsed by her husband Paresh Nath Mondal himself under his signature, who being alive was not examined as a witness in the instant suit for setting aside the compromise decree in the previous Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 and, as such, the initial onus to prove that the plaintiff did not put her left thumb impression on the petition of compromise in that suit was not at all discharged by the respondent No. 1 herein and thus the onus to disprove the plaintiffs case did not absolutely shift to the present defendant No. 1 on mere denial. The High Court Division having not considered this aspect committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision causing failure of justice.

5. It has been further argued that the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that summons of Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 was not served upon the plaintiff respondent No. 1 as defendant of that suit although there was a definite finding of the Appellate Court that summons were served upon her and, as such, judgment passed by the High Court Division is not a proper judgment of reversal. It is also argued that the learned Single Judge also failed to consider the question of limitation involved in a suit for setting aside the compromise decree in the backdrop of legal presumption that all official acts were done correctly, that the plaintiff failed to produce any evidence of possession of the suit land for more than 41 (forty-one) years.

6. We have perused the judgments of the courts below including the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. It appears that the High Court Division in the exercise of its revisional jurisdiction considered that the trial Court on consideration and assessment of evidence on record found that the plaintiff (respondent No. 1) has correctly asserted that the summons of earlier suit No. 182 of 1962 filed by original defendant was not served and the 'soleh' decree was obtained by practicing fraud and collusion.

<u>7. It appears that when the plaintiff respondent No. 1 disowned her thumb impression appearing in the alleged 'solenama' it was incumbent upon the original defendant, the predecessor of the leave-petitioners, to prove the thumb impression of the plaintiff respondent No. 1 by obtaining an expert opinion. The trial Court considered this aspect but the lower appellate Court as a final court of fact failed to consider the same and in such view of the matter we hold that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division having legally considered all aspects of the case based on material evidence on record rightly set aside the judgment of the lower appellate Court. We find no illegality has been committed by the High Court Division. The High Court also noticed that the plaintiff respondent No. 1 asserted that no summons of Title Suit No. 182 of 1962 filed by the original defendant No. 1 were served upon her and by this assertion of denial the onus has thus then shifted to the original defendant No. 1 (predecessor of the petitioners) and it was then incumbent upon him (defendant No. 1) to rebut the plaintiffs' said assertion by cogent evidence on record. The learned Single Judge, in our view, has rightly held to the effect that in the facts and circumstances of the case the onus shifted on the defendant No. 1 to show that the summons of the earlier suit was served on the plaintiff. This will not be enough and the defendant will have to further prove that the 'Soleh' decree was not obtained by practicing fraud and collusion.</u>

<u>8. Having regard to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case the finding of the lower appellate Court that the plaintiff put her thumb impression on the 'Solenama' is not correct and the High Court Division has rightly found that the finding of the appellate Court as regard the allege thumb impression of the plaintiff has been based on conjecture.</u>

<u>Mr. Md Nowab Ali, the learned Advocate-on-Record, could not pinpoint any legal infirmity or illegality on any account in the judgment of the learned Single Judge while reversing the finding of the lower appellate Court. In view of what has been discussed above we find no substance in the points raised in this petition and those merit no consideration. Hence this petition is dismissed.</u>

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 318-319 of 2000
lawyer:
Md Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nowab Ali, Advocate-on-Record -For the Petitioners. 	
Md Mozaffar Hossain, Advocate instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record -For Respondent No. 1
Not represented-Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Obeda Khatun and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Jaheda Khatun and anr ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 7-5-2000 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 6853 of 1991 & Civil Revision No. 6813 of 1991).
full_judgment:
Syed JR Mudassir Hussain J: These two Civil Petitions for leave to appeal by the two sets of defendants are from the common Judgment and order dated 7-5-2000 passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 6853 of 1991 and Civil Revision No. 6813 of 1991 discharging both the Rules heard analogously.

2. In Civil Petition No. 318 of 2000 the defendant No. 1, Obeda Khatun and six others are the petitioners herein whereas in Civil Petition No. 319 of 2000 Md Rejaul Hoque Fakir is another sole defendant petitioner. Most Jaheda Khatun is the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 in both the petitions. Since common facts and an identical question of law are involved between the said parties in respect of the selfsame property both the petitions have been heard together and this single judgment will govern both of them. The relevant facts in Civil Petition No. 318 of 2000 are that on 24-9-1984 the said plaintiff-respondent No. 1 Most. Jaheda Khatun instituted Title Suit No. 249 against the petitioners and proforma defendant-respondent No. 2 Abdus Sobhan in the court of the then First Court, Bogra for declaration of Title and recovery of the suit premises stating, inter alia, that the suit property was purchased by Chaturbhuj Kautia and others from the original owner Kajem Uddin Tarafdar and his sons Ekram and Ebadat by registered sale deed, that while Chaturbhuj Kautia was in possession of suit land, the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 took settlement of the land from the aforesaid purchaser Chaturbhuj Kautia by a registered patta dated 19-11-1955 on payment of Taka 2950 as Najrana and took possession thereof; that the MRR Khatian in respect of the suit land has been published in the name of the respondent No. 1; that thereafter, she constructed some shops on the suit land; that the predecessor of petitioner Nos. 1-6 took lease of shop No. 3 on monthly rent by executing a lease agreement for a period of 5 (five) years; that the petitioner's said predecessor defaulted in payment of the rent and also sub-let a portion of the suit premises in favour of petitioner No. 7 in violation of the lease agreement and for which the respondent No. 1 instituted a SCC suit against the predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 1-6 and petitioner No. 7; that since the SCC suit involved a complicated question of title same was withdrawn and hence the instant suit was filed.

3. The predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 1-6 and petitioner No. 7 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material facts of right, title and possession of respondent No. 1 contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable, it is bad for defect of parties and barred by limitation and adverse possession; that the petitioner No. 7 got his share in the suit premises by a registered deed of exchange, he will get more share in the suit premises than what he is now possessing land; that one Moslem Uddin Khondakar instituted a partition suit No. 181 of 1984 in the court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra in respect of the selfsame property praying for partition by metes and bounds. In the said partition suit the petitioner No. 7 was impleaded as plaintiff No. 2 and the respondent No. 1 was impleaded as defendant No. 28, that the petitioners were never a tenant of respondent No. 1; that the respondent No. 1 has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit premises and that the suit is liable to be dismissed and upon the above pleading the suit proceeded.

4. During the progress the petitioners filed an application on 29-5-1985 under sections 10 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Court of the then learned Munsif, First Court, Bogra praying for staying the further proceedings of the present suit till disposal of the aforesaid Partition Suit No. 181 of 1984 as the matter in issue is directly and substantially the same in both the suits and the parties are also common therein.

5. The learned Munsif by his order dated 8-6-85 rejected the said application for stay; against the aforesaid order the petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 237 of 1985 under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before the High Court Division, Rangpur Bench and obtained a Rule and an order of stay of further proceeding of the suit till the disposal of the aforesaid partition suit by the order dated 10-7-1985 and also called for the record of the present Title Suit No. 249 of 1984; that subsequently the said Civil Revision Case was renumbered as Civil Revision 6853 of 1991 (Dhaka).

6. In Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 319 of 2000 facts are that on 26-9-1984 the same plaintiff-respondent No. 1 instituted Other Class Suit No. 251 of 1984 in the court of the then Munsif, First Court, Bogra against the petitioners and proforma respondent No. 2 Md Tozammal Hossain for declaration of title and recovery of possession of the suit premises on the similar averment made out in Civil Petition No. 318 of 2000.

7. The defendant-petitioner Rezaul Hoque Fakir contested the said suit by filing a written statement and made similar statement made in the written statement filed by the aforesaid defendant-petitioner Nos. 1-6 and 7 of that Title Suit and the petitioner also asserted that he was never a tenant of plaintiff-respondent No. 1, that one Moslem Uddin Khondakar and another instituted Partition Suit No. 181 of 1984 in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra in respect of the selfsame property praying for partition by metes and bounds and in the said suit the petitioner was impleaded as defendant No. 26 and the respondent No. 1 was impleaded as defendant No. 28 and the suit is liable to be dismissed.

8. During the progress of the suit the defendant-petition filed an application on 5-5-1985 under sections 10 and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the court of the then learned Munsif, First Court, Bogra praying for staying the further proceedings of the suit till disposal of Partition Suit No. 181 of 1984 as the matter in issue is directly and subsequently the same and the parties also common therein.

9. The learned Munsif by the order dated 7-5-1985 rejected the petitioners' application for stay and against the said order the petitioner preferred Civil Revision No. 208 of 1985 under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before the High Court Division, Rangpur Bench and obtained a Rule and an order staying the further proceeding of the instant suit till the disposal of the aforesaid partition suit by the order dated 13-6-1985, subsequently, the said Civil Revision was renumbered as Civil Revision No. 6813 of 1991 (Dhaka); that both aforesaid Civil Revisions were heard together by a Single Bench of the High Court Division who discharged both the Rules and vacated the order of stay by the impugned judgment and order dated 4-2-1999.

10. The aforesaid two sets of defendants being aggrieved filed these two leave petitions against the common plaintiff-respondent No. 1.

11. Mr. Md Fazlul Karim, the learned Counsel appearing for both the leave-petitioners argued that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed an error. of law in failing to appreciate the provisions of section 10 and section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure that the issues involved in the Title Suit No. 249 of 1984, Title Suit No. 251 of 1984 and partition Suit No. 181 of 1984 are directly and substantially the same and the parties in the aforesaid suits are also common and unless the further proceedings of the aforesaid two suits are stayed till disposal of the Partition Suit No. 181 of 1984, there is every chance of conflicting decision which would result in serious miscarriage of justice.

<u>12. We have heard the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioners of both leave-petitions and perused the order of the learned Assistant Judge as well as the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. The present two Title Suits are for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession and the Partition Suit No. 181 of 1984 was filed by one Moslem Uddin Khondoker, are ex facie two different kinds of suit, and there cannot be the same issue in the said suits. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the materials on record rightly found that the nature and character of the instant Title Suits and the partition Suit No. 181 of 1984 are different in their nature and character and the issues involved therein are also different. In the aforesaid circumstances, we are of the view that an application for stay of the further proceeding of the plaintiff-respondents' two suits till disposal of the partition suit was rightly rejected by the learned Assistant Judge. The High Court Division, in our view, has also taken a correct view agreeing with the findings and decisions arrived at by the learned Assistant Judge.</u>

In the aforesaid premises, we hold that the learned Single Judge has committed no illegality in passing the impugned judgment to warrant our interference. Accordingly, these petitions are dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
Md Fazlul Karim, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellant. 
NI Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondent.
parties:
Md Golam Rasul ------ Appellant
Vs.
Chan Mohammad ------ Respondent
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated February 19, 1998 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 577 of 1991)
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This appeal, by leave, is by the plaintiff against the judgment and order dated February 19, 1998 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 577 of 1991 reversing the judgment and decree dated January 31, 1991 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Natore, in Title Appeal No. 124 of 1989 decreeing the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree dated May 30, 1989 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Na tore, in Other Class Suit No. 112 of 1979 dismissing the same. The suit was filed seeking declaration of title in and recovery of possession of 4½, decimals of land, shown in the sketch map attached to the plaint, part of 22 decimals of land of the 'kha' schedule which is part of the land of 'ka' schedule.

2. Plaintiff-appellant filed the suit stating that 45 decimals of land described in 'ka' schedule which comprises also the land of 'kha' schedule, belonged to Yakub Ali and he sold the same to his son Ishaque on May 12, 1977 who while in possession of the land of 'ka' schedule sold the same to the plaintiff on December 1, 1977. Plaintiffs case is that land in suit is of plot No. 1063 (old plot No. 1330) as described in the 'Kha' schedule. The plaintiff out of the said land has prayed for recovery of possession of 4½ decimals of land possessed by the defendant, respondent herein. It is the case of the appellant that at the time of purchase he requested the respondent to vacate the said 4½ decimals of land by removing the structures therein and he initially agreed to vacate the land, but later on did not.

3. Defendant-respondent contested the suit stating, inter alia, that land of 'kha' schedule belonged to his father Yakub Ali and that he was allowed by his father to stay in the land in suit and thereupon he is possessing the land by erecting huts. It was also the case of the defendant-respondent that plaintiff's vendor Ishaque never possessed the land in suit.

4. Initially, by the judgment and decree dated December 30, 1981 the suit was dismissed by the trial Court on the finding the defendant has been possessing the land in suit with the permission of his father Yakub Ali and the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was not acted upon and the plaintiff failed to prove exclusive title and possession of his vendor. On appeal, Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984, the judgment and decree of the trial Court was set aside and the case was sent back on remand to the trial Court with the direction to the plaintiff to amend the plaint suitably to convert the suit to a suit for partition for enabling the plaintiff to get some relief in the suit. The appellate Court found that defendant and his brother Ishaque had inherited the land in suit from their father Yakub Ali and in case the deed of Ishaque in favour of the plaintiff if not valid in respect of entire land so sold, even then the said kabala may be valid to the extent of share of Ishaque inherited from his father.

5. After the remand the trial Court dismissed the suit holding that plaintiff is entitled to 13 decimals of land which his vendor Ishaque was entitled out of the land in suit; that the suit was not maintainable since no prayer for partition was made as per direction of the appellate Court made in remanding back the suit.

6. On appeal the suit was decreed. The appellate Court decreed the suit on the finding that kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was acted upon and that defendant is in possession of the land measuring 4½ decimals in pursuance of permission from his father Yakub Ali and Yakub Ali was alive till 1977 and, as such, there is no scope to consider the kabalas executed both by Yakub Ali and Ishaque are fraudulent.

7. The defendant moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division set aside the judgment of the appellate Court upon making the Rule absolute and restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the finding that plaintiff did not amend the plaint in compliance with the direction of the appellate Court and the plaintiff did not amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition as was directed by the appellate Court by the judgment and order dated January 1,1986 made in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984 and, as such, as the trial Court dismissed the suit quite correctly the appellate Court without reversing the finding of the trial Court in that respect was in error in decreeing the suit.

8. Leave was granted to consider the submissions that the lower appellate Court as arrived at a clear finding as to the title of the plaintiff on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary, and also as arrived at a finding that defendant No. 1 has no claim in the land in dispute other than being a licensee from his father on the same and, as such, liable to be evicted by the plaintiff from the suit land, the learned Judge of the High Court Division was in error in not taking into consideration the aforesaid findings of the appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the said Court; that the learned Judge of the High Court Division was in error in making the Rule absolute only on a consideration that the plaintiff did not comply with the order earlier passed by the lower appellate Court while sending the suit back on remand.

9. The undisputed position is that land measuring 45 decimals described in the 'ka' schedule belonged to Yakub Ali. He sold the same in March 12, 1977 to his son Ishaque who sold said 45 decimals of land to the plaintiff-appellant on December 1, 1977. Since defendant was in occupation of 4½ decimals of land, shown in the sketch map attached to the plaint, part of 22 decimals of land of plot No. 1063 (new), 1330 (old), fully described in 'Kha' schedule and the defendant having not surrendered possession in favour of the plaintiff in fulfilment of his earlier commitment, as asserted by the plaintiff, he filed the suit for recovery of possession of 4½ decimals of land. The case of the defendant was that his father allowed him to stay in the land in respect whereof the decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession has been prayed by the plaintiff and he is possessing the land by erecting a hut. It was also his case that the kabala executed and registered by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was not acted upon. It may be mentioned while plaintiff filed the suit seeking declaration of title and recovery of khas possession Yakub Ali had died. The suit initially was dismissed by the trial Court as stated herein before and on appeal the Court upon allowing the appeal remanded the suit back to the trial Court with the direction to the plaintiff to amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition.

10. The trial Court again dismissed the suit on the finding that out of the suit land the plaintiff is entitled to 13 decimals of land to which his vendor Ishaque was entitled and further held that the suit was not maintainable since no prayer for partition was made upon making necessary amendment of the plaint suitably to a suit for partition as was directed by the appellate Court. Thereupon, the appellant filed an appeal and the appellate Court decreed the suit on the finding that the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was acted upon and the defendant is in possession of the land in suit ie 4½, decimals of land in pursuance of the permission of his father and Yakub Ali was alive till 1977 and, as such, there is no scope to say that the kabala executed and registered by Yakub Ali and Ishaque are fraudulent. As against the judgment of the appellate Court the defendant moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and the High Court Division set aside the judgment of the lower appellate Court on the ground that the plaintiff-appellant did not comply with the direction of the lower appellate Court to amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition.

11. The learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the lower appellate Court on the basis of the evidence, both oral and documentary, held that by the kabala of March, 1977 Yakub Ali transferred his entire land measuring 45 decimals in favour of his son Ishaque and said kabala was acted upon and the lower appellate Court also held since Yakub Ali was alive till 1977, as such, the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque and the kabala executed by Ishaque in favour of the plaintiff cannot be considered fraudulent. It is seen from the judgment of the trial Court that the said Court dismissed the suit primarily on the consideration that the plaintiff-appellant did not amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition as was directed by the appellate Court while remanding the suit back to the trial Court and the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was not acted upon and consequently, plaintiff was entitled to 13 decimals of land which Ishaque inherited from his father. No material was brought on record from the side of the defendant to establish the case as found by the trial Court that the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was not acted upon and consequently the finding of the trial Court that Ishaque had acquired interest to the extent of 13 decimals of land in his father's property measuring 45 decimals and, as such, plaintiff is entitled to the said quantity of land is based on no material. It has further been submitted by the learned Counsel that Yakub Ali transferred the entire quantity of land measuring 45 decimals to his son Ishaque and thereafter he transferred the land so got from his father to the plaintiff and there being no material that the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was not acted upon, as such, direction for amending the plaint suitably to a suit for partition as was made by the appellate Court made in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984 was apparently an error and, as such, non-compliance thereof in no way disentitled the appellant from having a decree as prayed for, if the same is available on the materials on record. Since on the materials on record the plaintiff was found to be entitled to a decree sought for in the suit and the same having been passed by the lower appellate Court the High Court Division and the trial Court were in error in dismissing the suit merely on the ground that plaintiff did not comply with the direction of the lower appellate Court made in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984 to amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition. In the background of the materials on record it is seen that the appellate Court was in serious error while made the order of remand in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984 directing the plaintiff to amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition since Yakub Ali exhausted his entire interest in the land as described in the 'ka' schedule part of which has been described in 'kha' schedule by the kabala of March 1977 and, as such, there was no scope or occasion for Ishaque or the defendant to inherit any land on the death of Yakub Ali and also there is no occasion for seeking partition of the land of the 'ka' schedule part of which as has been described in 'kha' schedule since partition is sought against the co-sharers, but Ishaque and defendant, both sons of Yakub Ali, were not the co-sharers of the land as described in the 'ka' schedule as well as in the 'kha' schedule.

<u>12. It has been submitted on behalf of the respondent while supporting the judgment of the High Court Division, that the High Court Division did not commit any error in restoring the judgment of the trial Court upon reversing the judgment of the appellate Court since direction of the appellate Court as was made in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984 to amend the plaint was not complied with. We have already found that the direction to amend the plaint made by the appellate Court was totally an erroneous one and in that view of the matter we are of the view that non-compliance of the said direction did in no way disentitle the appellant in having the relief sought for in the suit as allowed by the appellate Court in Title Appeal No. 124 of 1989. The High Court Division was in serious error in setting aside the judgment of the appellate Court since the said Court on the basis of the materials on record found that the reliefs prayed for are very much available to the plaintiff without amending the plaint suitably to a suit for partition as was directed by the appellate Court in its judgment passed in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984. In our view, while on the basis of the materials as are on the record the relief as prayed for can very much be given to the plaintiff, then for mere non-compliance of the direction of the appellate Court while, at one time, sending the suit back on remand to the trial Court directing the plaintiff to amend the necessary amendment' in the plaint seeking relief of different nature from the relief prayed for by the plaintiff apparently erroneous then the Court is quite competent to grant the relief sought for by the plaintiff in spite of non-compliance of the direction of the Court to amend the plaint for enabling him to get a different relief and thereupon to decree the suit instead of dismissing the suit for non-compliance of the direction of the Court which was otherwise erroneous. The plaintiff-appellant filed the suit seeking declaration of title and recovery of possession in respect of 4½ decimals of land out of 22 decimals of land as described in the 'kha' schedule of the plaint. The said 22 decimals of land is part of the 45 decimals of land as described in 'ka' schedule. The appellate Court on due consideration of the evidence on record held acquisition of title by the plaintiff from Ishaque who got the same from Yakub Ali is quite valid and the defendant as was a mere licensee of Yakub Ali and, as such, on the asking of the appellant he was to surrender possession in favour of the appellant and having not had surrendered possession the plaintiff sought for the reliefs in the suit as mentioned hereinbefore. The High Court Division set aside the judgment and decree of the appellate Court only on the ground plaintiff did not comply with the direction of the appellate Court as was made in Title Appeal No. 98 of 1984 to amend the plaint suitably to a suit for partition and restored the judgment of the trial Court dismissing the suit, The lower Appellate Court on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary, has found title of the plaintiff in the land in suit and also has held that the defendant was a mere licensee of his father in the land in suit. It was the contention of the defendant that the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of his son Ishaque was not acted upon. The lower appellate Court in the background of the facts as well as on the basis of the evidence held that the kabala executed by Yakub Ali in favour of Ishaque was acted upon. The High Court Division has not disturbed the findings so arrived at by the appellate Court in decreeing the suit. The learned Advocate-on-record for the respondent could also not point out any infirmity in the findings of the appellate Court on the basis whereof he decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff.</u>

13. In the background of the discussions made hereinabove we find merit in this appeal.

14. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

15. Accordingly, Judgment of the High Court Division is set aside and the judgment and decree of the appellate Court is restored.

There is no order as to costs.

End.

lawyer:
Mustafa Neaz Muhammad, Advocate, instructed by Abu Shiddique, Advocate-on-Record--For the Appellant. 
Rabi Shankar Chakraborty, Advocate, (appeared with the leave of the Court) instructed by AKM Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record—For Respondent No. 1. 
Respondent Nos. 2-45 — Not represented.
parties:
Rasheda Begum ------ Appellant
Vs.
MM Nurussafa and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated January 13, 2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2385 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: The appeal, by leave, is by the defendant No. 1 against the judgment and order dated January 13, 2002 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division passed in Civil Revision No. 2385 of 2001 disposing of the Rule obtained therein with the observation that the defendant-petitioner shall be at liberty to file a fresh application under section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the point of res-judicata and the trial Court shall frame one of the issues as to whether the suit is barred by res-judicata and will decide the issues after recording evidence of the parties.

2. Facts, in short, are that the appellant as plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 seeking separate Saham upon partition of 4.52½ acres of land. The claim for partition and Saham was made as one of the legal heirs of late Osiur Rahman. The suit was decreed on 15-5-1989. Two (2) Miscellaneous Cases, Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 1989 and Miscellaneous Case No. 44 of 1989 were filed under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking setting aside of the decree passed in the aforesaid suit, but the Miscellaneous Cases were dismissed. The petitioner of the Miscellaneous case No. 44 of 1989 took appeal, Miscellaneous Appeal No. 378 of 1990 to the High Court Division and the same was dismissed on 7-7-1994. A petition for leave to appeal, Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 120 of 1994 was filed before the Appellate Division and the same was dismissed for default on January 21, 1994. Decree in preliminary form passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 was made final. Thereupon Execution Case No. 1 of 1996 was filed. At that stage defendant No. 3 of Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1996 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking setting aside of the decree on the ground of non-service of summons upon him.

3. The Miscellaneous case was opposed by the appellant and the same was dismissed being time barred. The said defendant i.e. respondent No. 1 then filed other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 (partition) (previously numbered 96 of 1998) in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Cox's Bazar seeking declaration that the judgment and decree dated 15-5-1989 (decree signed on 22-5-1989), in other Class Suit No. 37, 1987 and the final decree dated 9-1-1997-passed in the aforesaid suit be set aside and also prayed for a separate saham in respect of the property described in the 'ga' schedule within the 'kha' schedule property. The appellant filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint of the other class suit No. 41 of 2000 primarily stating that the properties of the other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 and the other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 are common and the subject matter of the subsequent suit and the issues involved therein are same and similar to that of other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 and that because of the decree in the Other Class suit No. 37 of 1987 the Suit filed by the plaintiff (respondent No. 1) is barred by res-judicata.

4. The application so filed was opposed by the respondent No. 1 (plaintiff of the other class suit No. 41 of 2000). The learned Subordinate Judge by the order dated January 21, 2001 (order No. 37 dated 21-1-2001) rejected the application so filed under Order VII. rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure upon observing that the land which was the subject matter of the earlier suit and the land which is the subject matter of the present suit are not common and the parties are also not common and the issues of the earlier suit and the issues involved in the instant suit are not common and the cause of action of the earlier suit and the instant suit are not common and that matter that constitute res-judicata are absent and, as such, the instant suit is not barred by res-judicata.

5. The appellant as against the order of the Court of Joint District Judge moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2385 of 2001 and the High Court Division disposed of the Rule with the observation as stated hereinbefore. The leave was granted to consider the submissions that the appellant obtained decree in the previously instituted Partition Suit No. 37 of 1987 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Cox's Bazar admittedly in respect of the 'ka' schedule land of other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge and the plaintiff of the instant suit as was the defendant No. 3 in the previous suit and as he was unsuccessful up to the Appellate Division in getting the decree passed in the earlier suit set aside, as such the High Court Division erred in law in not rejecting the plaint of the other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 at least with respect of 'ka' schedule property of the instant suit, that the High Court Division was in error in not holding that on the averments made in the plaint of Other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 as the relief prayed for in the schedule 'ka' i.e. seeking setting aside of the preliminary' decree as well as the final decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 , were upheld up to the Appellate Division and, as such, relief so sought in prayer 'ka' of the present Suit No. 41 of 2000 is barred by the principle of res judicata.

6. The learned Counsel for the appellant submits that undisputed position is that the respondent No. 1, plaintiff in the suit, other class Suit No. 41 of 2000, in prayer 'ka' has prayed for setting aside of the preliminary decree dated 15-5-1989 and the final decree dated 9.1.1996 passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987. It is also the undisputed position that respondent No. 1 was defendant No. 3 in other class Suit No. 37 of 1987 and he filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1996 (under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure) seeking setting aside of the preliminary decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 and that the same was rejected on the ground of limitation by the trial Court. The order of rejection was maintained up to the Appellate Division. In the background of the said undisputed position the learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the property which was the subject matter of other class Suit No. 37 of 1987 as has also been made subject matter of the instant suit ie. Other class suit No. 41 of 2000 and that because of the decree passed in respect of the property which was the subject matter of the Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987, any subsequent suit is barred by res-judicata. He also submits that decree that was passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 having been challenged by the respondent No. 1 and as was unsuccessful up to the Appellate Division the instant suit seeking setting aside of decree passed in the earlier suit is not only barred by res-judicata but also barred because of the settled principle of law that there should be finality of the litigation after adjudication by the superior Court and, as such, finality so reached cannot be allowed to be re-agitated in the subordinate Court for the sake of discipline in the judicial arena. The learned Counsel for the appellant submits that plaint so far the same relates to the subject matter of Other Class suit No. 37 of 1987 or, in other words, relief as sought in the prayer 'ka' of the plaint, is liable to be rejected and that the plaint needs to be rejected so far the same, as evidenced by the relief 'ka' sought in the suit, relates to the subject matter of the earlier suit i.e. Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court. To substantiate this particular submission the learned Counsel has referred to the case of Guiness Peat (Trading) Limited vs Md Fazlur Rahman reported in 1992 BLD (AD) 247 = 44 DLR (AD) 242 and the case of Abdul Jalil and others vs Islamic Bank Bangladesh Ltd reported in 2000 BLD (AD) 278 = 52 DLR (AD) 12 wherein it has been held that in exceptional cases the Court may recourse to the provision of section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and can reject the plaint.

7. The learned Counsel for the respondent No. 1 submits that the question of res-judicata being a mixed question of fact and law can only be finally decided upon recording evidence of the parties and; as such, before recording of evidence a plaint on the plea of res-judicata is not liable to be rejected upon taking the statement made in support of the prayer for rejection of the plaint by the defendant. The learned Counsel in support of the aforesaid submission has referred to the case of Pushpa Rani Das and another vs. AKM Habibur Rahman and others reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 217 and the case of Mahbubul Huq vs. Md A Kader Munshi and others reported in 52 DLR 194.

8. The respondent No. 1 has filed Other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 seeking primarily 2 reliefs, first prayed for setting aside the decrees, both the preliminary and the final, passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987. The land sought to be partitioned in the earlier suit was 4.52½ acres. In that suit respondent No. 1 was the defendant No. 3. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 others who were defendants in the other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 filed Miscellaneous Cases under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree passed in the aforesaid suit but were unsuccessful up to the Appellate Division.

9. Ongoing through the materials on record it is apparent that defendants of the earlier suit were all out to deprive the plaintiff of the said suit of the fruit of the decree and that as the last resort has filed the Other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 seeking the relief primarily by way of setting aside the decrees that were passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 under the shadow of the relief seeking separate saham in respect of the 'ga' schedule land which is part of the land described in the 'kha' schedule. It is seen from the materials on record that the land which was the subject matter of Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 has also been made subject matter of the Other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000. It is pertinent to mention that none of the defendants of the Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 has challenged the final decree passed therein.

10. In Other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 relief has been sought for setting aside the decrees that were passed in other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987, although earlier the respondent No. 1 and others initiated proceedings to get the preliminary decree passed in the said suit set aside but they were unsuccessful up to the Appellate Division. In that state of the matter we are of the view that for the necessity of maintaining discipline in the judicial arena and that also for the sake of certainty of the result obtained in a suit or that for the purpose of termination of a dispute or difference at a certain stage or at certain time, person, who filed the subsequent suit if was a party in the earlier suit and tested the validity of the decree passed in the earlier suit but was unsuccessful, in the said situation he should not be allowed to proceed with the litigation, like the instant one, or in other words, the subsequent suit wherein he figured as plaintiff, so far the same relates to the subject matter of the earlier suit.

11. It is not disputed from the side of the respondent No. 1 that the relief sought for in prayer 'ka' of Other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 relates to seeking setting aside of the decrees passed in Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987. The relief so sought is not legally available since the decree passed in the said suit already reached finality on being challenged by the respondent No. 1 and others. In the background of the facts stated hereinbefore and the discussions made hereinabove we are of the view that the subsequent suit so far the same relates to the subject matter of the earlier suit ie. Other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987, should not be allowed to proceed with for preventing abuse of the process of the Court.

<u>12. The law is more or less settled that matter of rejection of plaint is not confined to the provision of Order XI rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In a fit or appropriate case i.e. while the proceeding initially is an abuse of the process of the Court or a contrive to achieve something which the party failed upon proceeding under the law provided for or in any other case akin to cases as mentioned above, the Court taking recourse of the provision of section 151 would be competent to reject the plaint or struck out part of the relief prayed for or sought in a subsequent suit.</u>

<u>In that view of the matter we are of the opinion continuation of the suit i.e. other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000, as regard the matter that was an issue in the earlier suit, i.e. other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987, wherein the respondent No. 1 was a party, should not be allowed being an abuse of the process of the Court. The statements made in the plaint of other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 in support of the prayer 'ka' are liable to be struck out and the same are struck out and consequently matter (s) that was the subject matter of other Class Suit No. 37 of 1987 shall not be the subject matter of the Other Class Suit No. 41 of 2000 and shall also not be a subject matter for adjudication in the other Class suit No. 41 of 2000. In the result the appeal is allowed with costs.</u>

End.
