M Faziul Karim with Mahbubey Alam and Md. Harun-Ar-Rashid, Advocates — For the Appellant.
Lutfur Rahman Mondal with Md. Abdus Samad Kamal, Advocates — For the Respondents.
parties:
Nilufa Begum ----- Appellant
Vs.
Md. Atash Ali and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Sirajul Islam J: This appeal by the plaintiff is directed against the judgment and decree dated 21-4-1993 and 26-4-1993 passed by Subordinate Judge 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 dismissing the plaintiff's suit on the preliminary issue of maintainability.

2. The appellant Mst. Nilufa Begum as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 in the court of Subordinate Judge 1st Court, Dhaka against the defendant Md. Atash Ali and others for a declaration of plaintiff's right, title and interest in the suit land by treating the impugned final decree dated 16-6-1980 passed in Title Suit No.92 of 1966 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka as fraudulent, illegal, nullity and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that the piece and parcels of land measuring 0.53 decimals in different plots described in the schedule to the plaint along with other lands originally belonged to one Sk. Emminat who while owning and possessing the same died leaving behind his only son Sk. Himmat as his sole heir to inherit the suit land. That the plaintiff's father Sekandar Ali Bepari purchased the suit land from some lineal descendants of Sk. Himmat vide registered kabala dated 7-10-63. One Suburjan Bibi and 2 others filed Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 for partition of the suit land and other land impleading the plaintiff's father Sk. Sekandar Ali Bepari as defendant No. 42. Defendant contested Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 in the court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court; Dhaka by filing a written statement claiming his share as a co-sharer in the suit land by purchase. Considering the facts, circumstances and the evidence of the case, the learned Subordinate Judge, decreed the Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 on contest against contesting defendant No. 42 Sekandar Ali Bepari and ex parte against the rest in the preliminary form by his judgment and decree dated 23-11-1968.

3. Against that judgment and decree of the Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 that Sekandar Ali Bepari (defendant r 42), the father of the present plaintiff, preferred first appeal No. 95 of 1969 in this court. During the pendency of the appeal in this court, the sole appellant Sekandar Ali died on 19-10-77. Thereafter, the heirs of Sekandar Ali appeared by power and filed an application for their substitution in place of their deceased predecessor Sekandar Ali and accordingly, they were substituted by order dated 12-1-1978 and thus they proceeded with the appeal. Ultimately, after hearing both the parties, the first Appeal No.95 of 1969 was dismissed by judgment dated 20-4-1979. After disposal of the appeal, record of Title Suit No.92 of 1966 went back to the trial Court and then the learned Subordinate Judge through usual process made the preliminary decree final by judgment and decree dated 16-6-1980.

4. Thereafter the present plaintiff Nilufa Begum filed the present Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 on 19-3-1987 and her main allegation in the plaint is that after the death of her father (defendant No. 42 of title Suit No. 92 of 1966) his heirs were substituted by the plaintiff showing this Nilufa Begum as major defendant No. 42(n) in spite of her being a minor at that time and that was done fraudulently at the instance of her step brother Habibur Rahman outside the knowledge of the plaintiff and of her mother and natural guardian who is still alive. That the plaintiff Nilufa Begum was not properly represented in that partition suit and hence the final decree passed on 16-6-1980 in that partition suit is a nullity and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff's further case is that the final decree was obtained against some dead persons also and that the decree is a nullity in that sense also. The plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land and that defendants are quite strangers in respect of the suit land. Although writ of delivery of possession in the final decree was issued but it was not actually executed on the spot The defendant has no right, title or possession in the suit land. The plaintiff had her possession on the suit land. The decree passed against her during her minority is not binding against the plaintiff. That the decree has clouded the plaintiffs title to the suit land and hence the plaintiff is now constrained to file the present suit No. 133 of 1987 for declaration as aforesaid.

5. During the proceeding of the suit, the defendants 1, 2, 4-17 filed an application under Order 7 rule 11 CPC for rejecting the plaint but that the learned Subordinate Judge had rejected that application for rejection of the plaint vide order dated 21-4-1987. Against that order, the defendant moved this court in Civil Revision No. 466 of 1987 and the Rule was discharged vide this Court's order dated 8-11-1990. Thereafter, the Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 was proceeding in the trial Court and during this period, the defendant Nos. 1-12 filed a further application under Order 14 rule 2 read with Order 15 rule 3(1, 2) CPC on 1-9-91 praying for framing an issue of maintainability and for dismissing the suit as being not maintainable in this form and accordingly, an issue of maintainability appears to have been framed by order dated 22-1-1992. Then after several adjournments this petition and the issue of maintainability was ultimately heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge on 21-4-1993. After hearing both the parties and considering the facts and circumstances relevant to the case, the learned Subordinate Judge allowed the defendant's application filed under Order 14 rule 2 read with Order 15 rule 3(1,2) CPC and dismissed the plaintiff's suit on the issue of maintainability vide his judgment and decree dated 21-4-1993 and 26-4-1993 respectively.

6. Being aggrieved by this judgment and decree dated 21-4-1993 and 26-4-1993, the plaintiff Nilufa Begum as appellant has preferred this first appeal No. 168 of 1993 in this court.

7. The defendant-respondents appeared by power and opposed this appeal.

8. The first point as urged by Mr. M. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant, is that the defendants earlier filed an application under Order 7 rule 11 CPC praying for rejection of the plaint but that the learned Subordinate Judge rejected this application vide order dated 21-4-1987 against which the defendants filed CR No. 466 of 1987 in this court and that this court after hearing the parties discharged the Rule in Civil Revision No. 466 of 1987 holding that the suit is not barred under Order 7 rule 11 CPC and, as such, the subsequent application filed by the defendants under Order 14 rule 2 read with Order 15 rule 3 (1, 2) is not maintainable in the face of the discharge order passed by this court in the earlier revision case, but that the learned Subordinate Judge without proper consideration of this fact, has allowed the subsequent application and illegally dismissed the plaintiff's suit on a preliminary point and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge are not sustainable in law. In this respect Mr. Lutfar Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondents has submitted that the earlier application as rejected by the learned Subordinate Judge and upheld by the High Court Division was not in respect of maintainability but that was a matter for rejection of the plaint only under Order 7 rule 11 CPC and more so while disposing the civil revision No. 466 of 1987 this court kept the question of maintainability open for consideration.

<u>9. From the above submissions as made by the learned Advocates for both the parties and the papers as are available in the paper book, it appears that the earlier matter was a quite different matter for rejection of the plaint under Order 7 rule 11 CPC and not a matter for maintainability under Order 14 rule 2 read with Order 15 rule 2(a)(2) CPC. It further appears from the impugned judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge that he had also noticed about the earlier matter of civil revision No. 466 of 1987 against the order of rejection of an application under Order 7 rule 11 CPC dated 21-4-1987 and found that matter being a different matter has not put any bar in the disposal of the matter of res judicata about maintainability in the suit. After considering all the facts and the lengthy circumstances involved in this case as per volume of papers as available herein, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge is justified in holding that there is no bar in disposing the question of res judicata and the maintainability of the suit under Order 14 rule 2 and read with Order 15 rule 3 (1)(2) CPC.</u>

<u>10. Next point urged by Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant, is that Sekandar Ali Bepari, the father of Nilufa Begum, died during the pendency of the First Appeal No. 95 of 1969 filed against the original preliminary decree of Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 and that while substituting the heirs of deceased Sekandar Ali (defendant 42 of Title Suit No. 92 of 1966) this Nilufa Begum was shown as a major in spite of the fact that she was a minor at that time and that she was show major fraudulently at the instance of her step-brother, Habibur Rahman in collusion with the defendants and similarly, she was shown as major while substituting them in Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 at the time of making the preliminary decree final and thus the plaintiff Nilufa Begum of the present suit was not properly represented nor had she any knowledge about her substitution as a major and the final decree thus obtained in Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 is a fraudulent decree and hence this final decree in question is a nullity and is not binding against the present plaintiff Nilufa Begum. The learned Advocate argued that the learned Subordinate Judge did not discuss the facts as per statement made by the plaintiff in her plaint nor considered the papers relevant therewith and thus he came to a wrong finding that the plaintiffs suit was not maintainable and was barred by res judicata and, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge is not sustainable in law.</u>

11. In this respect Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mandal, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondents, has drawn our attention to pages 77 and 82 of the Paper Book and said that after death of the said Sekandar Ali Bepari (defendant No.42 of No.92/66) during pendency of the first appeal No.95 of 1969 all his heirs including this Nilufa Begum voluntarily appeared by executing a power and filed an application for their being substituted in the appeal and accordingly, their prayer was allowed by the court in appeal and they were duly substituted by the court vide order dated 12-1-1978 and it also appears from the office note of this court that the vokalatnama was duly executed by all the heirs of the deceased Sekandar Ali and they had filed the application for substitution.

12. In the vokalatnama it appears that this Nilufa has signed her name at serial No.14 in the vokalatnama along with the name of her mother Jamila Khatun and other brothers. By a reading of the plaint as filed by Nilufa Begum in Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 it appears that not a single word has been stated about the signature of Nilufa as is there in the vokalatnama filed by all of them as heirs of their deceased father in this court. It is not stated in the plaint whether it was her signature or whether her signature was obtained by mis-representation. While his attention was drawn to this fact of the signature of Nilufa Begum along with her mother and brothers in the vokalatnama and in the application Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate for the appellant, said that the signature of Nilufa is neither denied nor affirmed. It has been simply stated in the plaint that substitution petition was made at the instance of her step-brother Habibur Rahman outside the knowledge of the plaintiff and her natural guardian mother who is still alive. But the fact remains that in this statement as made in the plaint also Nilufa did not deny her signature. On the other hand, her mother stated to be still alive has not made any statement or objection any where since the time of substitution on 12-1-1978 till to-day nor did she raise any objection in respect of this vokalatnama as filed therein. It appears that the same substitution of the some persons as per their own statement as made swearing in an affidavit in this court was made in the trial Court at the time of making the final decree. In this view of the matter, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge has rightly commented that at the time of substitution of this plaintiff Nilufa Begum along with other heirs of the deceased Sekandar Ali the plaintiffs of partition suit No. 92 of 1966 or for that matter the defendants of present Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 had no role to play. Therefore, the question of fraud by the defendants of the present suit does not arise. It was their own application on which the substitution was made. We fully agree with this observation as made by the learned Subordinate Judge while disposing of the plaintiffs Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 on the question of maintainability and res judicata.

13. Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the defendant -respondents, next referred to two misc. cases being Misc. Case No. 233 of 1980 filed by defendant No. 36 and Misc. Case No. 53 of 1981 filed by the heirs of defendant No.38 and defendant No.6 under section 47 CPC objecting the Title Execution Case No. 49 of 1980 filed after passing of the final decree of the partition suit and that in both the Misc. Cases the same point of fraud was raised by the petitioners saying that they were not properly represented and that the final decree was passed against some dead persons and that this Nilufa was shown major being a minor at the time of substitution of the heirs of deceased Sekandar Ali Bepari. The learned Advocate submits that both the Misc. cases were dismissed after full hearing and that the petitioners went upto the Appellate Division against the dismissal judgment passed analogously by the trial Court. The learned Advocate submits that this High Court Division affirmed the judgment holding that the substitution was made on a sworn statement of the heirs of the deceased defendant No. 42 and that this Nilufa or any one of them did not raise any objection against such statement made by themselves but now that point was raised only at the instance of other persons and that this finding of the High Court Division was upheld by the Appellate Division with the observation that this is a complete answer to the contention as put forward on behalf of the petitioners. Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mondal submits that this is a decision of the highest court and this decision has totally closed the question of alleged fraud in the substitution of Nilufa Begum along with all her co-heirs of deceased Sekandar Ali and that this decision of the highest court is binding on this court and Subordinate Court. We find that this is a decision of the Appellate Division of this Court while summarily rejecting the Civil petition for leave No.457 of 1982 filed by the petitioners of the above mentioned two Misc. Cases raising the question of minority of Nilufa Begum also. In the facts and circumstances and the papers as are available in the paper book we find that the question of fraud as raised by plaintiff Nilufa Begum in the matter of the substitution in TS No. 92 of 1966 has already been finally decided upto the highest Court and we think that there is no scope to reagitate that question again in the form of a fresh suit.

14. In this respect Mr. Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant, submits that Nilufa was not a party in that Misc. case Nos. 233 of 1980 and 53 of 1981 and as such the decision arrived at in these two misc. cases upto Appellate Division is not binding on Nilufa Begum. But the fact remains that Nilufa Begum's being a party or no party in the Misc Cases, the question of her minority was raised in those misc. case upto the Appellate Division and that the learned Appellate Division has answered that question and that answer is final. We do not find any scope for us to make any departure from that answer.

Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the defendant-respondents, referred to a case of 164 of 1985 filed by one Golapjan Bibi with the similar attempt of setting aside the final decree of partition suit No. 92 of 1966 on the selfsame ground of decree against dead persons and that she was not made party and that this Nilufa Begum being minor was shown to be major while substituting herein the suit. Subsequently, that Golapjan Bibi filed application for withdrawal of the suit and at that time defendant No.57 filed an application for transposition which was allowed by the Subordinate Judge and in revision being Civil Revision No.135 of 1987 this Court also discharged the Rule vide order dated 16-11-1989 against which the present defendant went to the Appellate Division in CA No. 40 of 1990 and the appeal was allowed and the order of the courts below were set aside and the petition for transposition filed by the defendant No.57 was rejected with the similar finding that the matter is closed and passed and the question as raised by defendant No.57 cannot be agitated as the matter was a closed and passed matter and then the suit was dismissed for non prosecution. Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mondal submits that all this is an unprecedented kind of prolognation of a litigation in respect of self same subject matter raised by different persons at different times and in different names coming upto the Appellate Division with the sole aim of undoing a final decree passed by Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 92 of 1966 and that the same process of prolongation is still continuing by the present plaintiff Nilufa but that there must be an end of such litigation.

<u>15. Considering all the above facts and circumstances of the case and the voluminous papers as are contained in the two paper books we find that only defendant No. 42, the predecessor of the present plaintiff, contested the partition suit No. 92 of 1966 and that she alone filed the FA No.95 of 1969 in which the preliminary decree was confirmed and thereafter the trial Court made the preliminary decree final after observing the due process of law and since thereafter the non-contesting defendants had filed different suits and Misc. Cases against the final decree on the selfsame ground and that the matter has been finally decided upto the Appellate Division of this court. After that final decision of the Appellate Division in respect of the same subject matter and on the same question, we do not find any further scope for us to go in the departure of that decision. We fully agree with the contention as put forward by Mr. Lutfur Rahman Mondal that this is an unprecedented kind of prolognation of a litigation in the self-same subject matter and there must be an end to such unnecessary and fruitless litigation.</u>

16. It is noticed from the facts and papers as available in this case that the plaintiff Subornnessa and two others of partition Suit No. 92 of 1966 claimed share in the suit property by way of inheritance and by purchase and after trial the learned Subordinate Judge rejected their claim of inheritance and allowed only the share of the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 8 acquired by purchase and it appears that the preliminary decree passed in the suit was a quite justified decree being upheld by this court in appeal filed by the sole contesting defendant No. 42. No other persons raised any step against that judgment and decree passed and confirmed in appeal by this court. We fail to understand how some non-contesting defendants and this plaintiff, a self substituted heir of the sole contesting defendant No. 42, can raise question of that confirmed judgment and decree one after another.

17. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge while dismissing the suit on point of law and fact of its maintainability and on res judicata has observed that after the preliminary decree confirmed by the High Court Division in appeal in presence of the present plaintiff Nilufa Begum along with all other heirs of deceased Sekandar Ali, the making of the preliminary decree into a final decree was a mere formality by the normal process of the court. We agree that the preliminary decree is made final by way of routine order after the receipt of the commission report, etc, and it appears that all the co-sharers were also parties in the making of the preliminary decree final. After all these stages, we do not find any right of Nilufa Begum to agitate the same question in the form of her independent suit.

18. Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate argued that had the First Appeal No. 95 of 1969 been allowed, this Nilufa would never go to raise any question of her minority or fraud or anything like that, after the dismissal of that appeal, it is simply an attempt made by her to undo a final decree passed after a long lapse of time the preliminary decree being confirmed in appeal filed by her own father. We agree with this contention of the learned Advocate that no such question would be raised had the appeal been allowed.

19. It may be mentioned here that principle of justice is that there must be an end to litigation but in the volume of facts and circumstances of this case starting from 1966 it appears that different attempts are being made by different persons to defeat a hard earned decree obtained by the original plaintiff Suburnnessa and 2 others in the partition Suit No. 92 of 1966 after a labour of about 25 years making a prolongation of a litigation in respect of same subject matter and same question which should not be allowed to continue.

<u>20. Considering all the above facts, circumstances and the papers and documents as are available in 2 paper books and the discussion as we have made above, we find that the learned Subordinate Judge is quite justified in putting an end to a fruitless Title Suit No. 133 of 1987 on the point of law of maintainability and the res judicata. We do not find anything for us to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Subordinate Judge, we find no substance in this appeal.</u>

In the result, the appeal is dismissed with normal costs plus a compensatory cost of Taka 5,000.00 (Taka five thousand) to be paid by the plaintiff-appellant to the contesting defendant-respondents.

End.

parties:
Chan Mahmood (Md) & others  ------ Petitioners
Vs
Md Hossain Ali being dead his heirs (Ka) Md Sekander Ali & ors ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued at the instance of the defendant against the impugned judgment and decree dated 16-2-95 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Tangail in OC Appeal No. 216 of 1990 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 16-6-1990 passed by the Assistant Judge, Madhupur in Other Suit 37 of 1987 for declaration of title decreeing the suit.

2. The suit of the plaintiff, in short, is that, Gowhar Sheikh was the original Raiyot having his 16 annas ownership over 12.42 acres land including the suit land comprising an area of 8.47 acres. The CS Khatian was correctly prepared in the name of said Gowhar Sk Plaintiffs are the successive heirs of Gowhar Sk According to them, the suit land devolved on them and they are in possession. The suit land is part of the land of CS Khatian 31(Ext). The CS Khatian has also been proved and exhibited by the defendants as Ext. C and by the plaintiff as Ext.1

3. Plaintiffs'' specific case is that, the land of CS Khatian 31 was divided into three ROR Khatians, that is SA Khatians being 28, 29 and 30. ROR Khatians 28 and 29 were wrongly prepared in the name of the defendants. Despite the same, the plaintiffs were in possession of the entire suit land of the said three ROR Khatians. Because of the preparation of said two Khatians 28 and 29 in respect of post of the suit land in favour of the defendants the title of the plaintiffs has been clouded. Therefore, they have filed the suit for declaration of their title alleging that in the month of Agrahayan, 1393 BS when they went to the local Tahsil office to pay rent they found that the said ROR Khatians have been wrongly prepared in the name of the defendants.

4. Defendants 1-4 contested. Defendants admitted the original rayoti right of Gowhar Sk in the suit land under the CS Khatian. Defendants also admitted the plaintiffs as successive heirs of said Gowhar Sk. Their specific case is that the suit land was auctioned sold in 1930 AD in Rent Realisation case No. 1051C of 1930. The original Zaminder of the suit Khatian Abdul Hamid Chowdhury of the Nagbari Estate, purchased the suit land in auction vide Ext. B, the sale certificate. He possessed and held the land for stipulated period for more than two years and thereafter the defendants took pattan of the suit land from said Abdul Hamid Chowdhury. Accordingly, the defendants, as alleged, have acquired their ownership in the suit land and are in possession on payment of land revenue althrough both to the Zamindar and to the Government.

5. Defendants denied the possession of the plaintiffs since alleged auction sale. They also assert that ROR Khatians were correctly prepared in their favour in consideration of their ownerships and possession of the suit land.

6. In this context, both parties adduced their respective evidence both oral and documentary.

7. Plaintiffs' exhibits are 1-1(a), 1(b), 1 (c), 2 part, 2(a)2 and 2(a), Defendants exhibits are A series, which are rent receipts showing payment of rent by them to the Zaminder and to the Government after state acquisition. Ext B is the Bainama (Sale Certificate) and Ext. C is the CS Khatian and C(2) is the ROR Khatian. These are the material exhibits from the side of both parties. Defendants could not file the pattannama or any documentary evidence as to their taking pattan from Abdul Hamid Chowdhury So also defendants failed to produce or file in the court the letter of delivery of possession to complete the alleged auction purchase of the suit auction by Abdul Hamid Chowdhury. The defendants also could not produce any paper or document to show that the suit land originally belonged to Nagbari Estate of Abdul Hamid Chowdhury.

<u>8. Both parties examined some witnesses adducing oral evidence to prove their possession which they claimed reciprocally. It is the settled principle of law that when the entire evidence come in the record the onus of proof is divided and splitted up academic.</u>

9. In this case, the plaintiffs' onus was to prove that they are the heirs of Gowhar Sk and they are in possession. The plaintiffs are admittedly successive heirs of Gowhar Sk. Defendants' onus was to prove the genuineness of the said auction sale of the suit property and that Abdul Hamid Chowdhury was the original Zaminder having rent receiving interest in the suit holding.

10. Defendants took the specific plea in para 16 of the written statement in the following averments:

“এমতাবস্থায় উপরোক্ত ওয়ারিশান এজমালিতে গহের শেথের সাকুল্য সম্পত্তিতে গহের শেথের ত্যাক্ত সাকুল্য ১২.৪৪ ডিং জমিতে এজমালিতে স্বত্ববান দথলকার থাকে। এজমালিতে দখলকার থাকার কারণে উক্ত জমির খাজনা বাকি পরিলে টাংগাইলের ১নং মুনসেফ আদালতে ১০৫১/ছি সন ১৯৩০ গং খাজনার মোকদ্দমা মূলে গহের শেখের ত্যাক্ত সাকুল্য ১২.৪৪ ডিং জমি নিলাম বিক্রি হয়। উক্ত আদালতে উক্ত প্রকার ১৯৩১ সনের ২৬১/ছি নং ডিক্রি জারী মোকদ্দমা মূলে নাগবাড়ী এস্টেটের মালিক জনাব আঃ হামিদ চৌধুরী সাহেব ডিক্রীদার হিসাবে নালিশী সি, এস ৩১ খাতয়ান ভূক্ত মং ১২.৪৪ ডিং জমি নিলাম খরিদ করিয়া দুই বৎসরের অধিককাল খাস দখলকার থাকেন।”

<u>11. So the defendants, according to the provision of sections 102, 103 and 104 of the Evidence Act, are to prove the original ownership of Abdul Hamid Chowdhury and that he was the decree holder in the rent suit and he made the purchase in the auction sale legally and he settled the suit land to the defendants.</u>

<u>12. Mr Halder, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff petitioners, reads the contents of Ext 1 vis-a-vis Ext.0 which is the CS Khatian to me which shows that the property originally did not belong to Abdul Hamid Chowdhury, rather, it belonged to one Shayam Chand Singh and under him Gowhar Sk was in possession as Raiyot. So, the specific case of the defendants as stated above is belied by the contents of Ext. 1 of the plaintiffs which is at the same time Ext. C of the defendants. Thus the plaintiffs succeeded in proving their moot case as to title and the defendants'' case cuts at the root of it.</u>

<u>13. The trial Court dismissed the suit finding, inter alia, that the auction sale was valid and the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession. Trial Court held that the defendants could prove that the suit land along with other lands of the said Khatian belonged to Nagbari estate and the suit land was auction sold and was legally purchased by said Abdul Hamid Chowdhury as the Original landlord and later on settled the same to the defendants. This finding of the trial Court is totally beyond the admitted basic title deed namely, the CS Khatian. Therefore, these findings of the trial Court are the result of misreading of evidence, it has been rightly rebutted by the appellate Court.</u>

14. Appellate Court has decided the dispute in a very slipshod manner. Appellate Court believed the possession of the plaintiffs and disbelieved the possession of the defendants as the last and final court of fact, considering the evidence both oral and documentary. Appellate Court rightly found that the defendants could not produce any paper as to the rent suit or execution case thereof and also admittedly the defendants could not file letter of delivery of possession. Although SA Khatian has been prepared in the name of the defendants, but the same cannot extinguish the title of the plaintiffs who are admittedly the heirs of the original owner said Gowhar Sk. Appellate Court also found that the defendants could not prove their pattan which is the anchor sheet of their case of title from said Abdul Hamid Chowdhury.

<u>15. Trial Court wrongly found that the suit in the present form for simple declaration was not maintainable. Because the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession, when the plaintiff could prove their possession as found by the appellate Court, the suit for declaration of title is very much maintainable.</u>

<u>16. Mr Ramzan Ali Khan, the learned Counsel for the defendant opposite parties, submits that the rent receipt of the defendants although are many in number, but the same were manufactured by forgery by the defendants to grab the suit land although they have no title or possession in the same. Defendants could not show payment of rent of the period from the years 1934-1943, 1945-46, 1950-52 and for the years 1976-87 which also destroys the case of the defendants that they paid rent for all the years from 1930, the alleged years of taking pattan of the suit land by them. Preparation of SA or ROR Khatian and payment of the rent does not create any title in favour of the defendants when the plaintiffs could prove their possession as well, in the suit land.</u>

17. Mr Ramzan Ali, the learned Counsel, rightly submits that because the defendants failed to produce any document as to their auction sale and specially letter of delivery of possession and patta as to settlement, the case of the defendant is hit by the provision of Order 21, rule 95 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his argument Mr Ali relies on the decision in the case of Salmat Ali and others vs. Ali Akbar, reported in AIR 1920 (Lahore) page 30 wherein their Lordships have held as under :

"Possession must be delivered in either of two methods provided by R 95 or R 96. Symbolical possession against judgment debtors who are parties to execution proceedings amount to actual possession".

Here in this case, there is nothing to show that the delivery of possession was taken by the auction purchasers namely, the zaminder. Lacking of delivery of possession has upset at the very root of the case of the defendants. Ext. 1 of plaintiffs is the Exts of the defendants which is the CS Khatian wherein there is nothing to show that Abdul Hamid Chowdhury was at all the previous zaminder having rent receiving interest in any portion of the suit land.

18. Mr Halder, the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that although there is no letter of delivery of possession after auction sale of the suit land, the sale certificate being a deed of title as held in 5 DLR 285 in the case of Kalipada Saha and others vs. Nitya Nanda Saha and others even without a letter of delivery of possession the title of the purchaser is complete and, as such, the appellate Court should have found that the defendants acquired good title. In the said decision it has been held by an eminent Judge of this sub-continent Mr Justice Ibrahim as follows :

"It is not a deed of title in the sense that it shows the creation of a new right".

<u>19. So, in view of the facts and circumstances as stated above, only the boinama Ext. B is not sufficient to decree the title in favour of the defendants. Genuineness of the rent receipts of the defendants are not beyond doubt and because of gap in payment of alleged rent by the defendants they also cannot stand on the footing claiming their title on the basis of adverse possession and no ground has been taken in this revision for adverse possession of the defendants. So, attempt of Mr Halder in this regard ended in futility. It is settled principle of law that when original claim of title is referable to certain documents adverse possession cannot be there (See 10 DLR (SC) 174). It has been found as follows :</u>

<u>"Possession is not adverse where original occupation is referable to lawful title".</u>

<u>Mr Halder relies on the decision in the case of Abdul Hamid and others vs. Abul Hossain Mir and others reported in 35 DLR 295 and submits that latter record of right will prevail over the earlier one and in that view, he submits that SA Khatian having been prepared in the name of the defendants it will prevail upon the CS Khatian. But his submission cannot be accepted because of the more important observation made in the same decision which is as follows :</u>

<u>"Presumption of the CS Khatian did not lose its weight because of absence of evidence as to its basis."</u>

<u>SA Khatian can create presumption of possession but not of title which the CS Khatian can. Both parties adduced oral evidence to prove possession. The appellate Court on appreciation of the same as the last and final court of fact has found the same in favour of the plaintiffs.</u>

20. Mr Halder also cites the decision in the case of Erfan Ali vs. Joynal Abedin Mia reported in 1983 BLD (AD) 342, wherein the Appellate Division has held as follows :

"Rent receipts their evidentiary value though not documents of title, they are important items of evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows title".

The possession itself can be used for collateral purpose in deciding title. So, possession follows title. Here in this case both title and possession have been found by the appellate Court in favour of the plaintiffs. This case is distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the said case. So that decision is not applicable in this instant case.

21. For the reasons and discussions made above, I find that the appellate Court although has passed his judgment in a very slipshod manner, but impliedly has rebutted the findings and decisions of the trial Court both as to the title and possession of the defendants with cogent and well founded legal reasons. Therefore, the appellate Court's judgment does not suffer from any illegality either in fact or in law resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

22. In the result, I find no merits in this revision and the Rule is liable to be discharged

23. In the result the Rule is discharged with costs. The suit is decreed. The judgment and decree of the appellate Court is upheld.

Send down the records to the courts below at once.

End.

full_judgment:
A M Mahmudur Rahman J : The petitioner obtained this Rule Nisi calling upon the respondents to show cause why the resolution dated 1-1-94 marked as 'ka' adopted by the Syndicate condemning and censuring the petitioner should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect.

2. The petitioner was elected as the Dean of the Faculty of Social Science and he took charge of the Faculty from the previous Dean Prof. Anwarullah Chowdhury on 31-7-93. In 1982 a new system of admission of students into 1st year Honours Course in the University was introduced. According to this system, the application for admission into 1st year Honours courses was divided in four groups, namely, (1) 'Ka' unit for Science and Biological Science, (2) 'Kha' Unit for Arts and Social Science, (3) 'Ga' Unit for Commerce and (4) 'Gha' unit for transfer from one branch of study to other. For such admissions Admission Committees were formed every year by the Vice-Chancellor of the University. The Deans of the Faculties are the Chairman of the Admission Committees. The General Admission Committee decided to realise fees for admission from the students seeking admission and the fund so collected by each Unit is to be administered and operated by the Chairman of each Admission Committee. The said fund is the fund of Admission Committee and was never treated as the fund of the University, nor it was ever reflected in the budget of the University and as audit was never done in respect of the said fund. The Admission Committee is the authority to deal with the fund and the Chairman of such Faculty was responsible for operation and to keep account of the fund, The Chairman is to submit amount of the fund to the Vice Chancellor at the end of his term. Prof. Anowarullah Chowdhury continued as Dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences till 29-7-93 and was Chairman of the Admission Committee of 'Gha' Unit. After his term was over the petitioner was elected for the term of 1993-94. He had to perform the business of the Admission Committee left over undone for the previous year 1992-93, from the date he took over charge of office of the Chairman of the Admission Committee. The Vice-Chancellor constituted on 30-12-93 an Admission Committee for 'Gha' Unit for the year 1993-94 with the petitioner as Chairman. The petitioner took charge of the fund and found irregularity in the management of the same during the term of the previous Chairman Prof. Anowarullah Chowdhury and he was requested by the petitioner to hand over papers relating to the fund to him. But Prof. Anowarullah Chowdhury did not hand over the papers to the petitioner and accordingly the petitioner felt the necessity for auditing the fund by a Chartered Accountant. For such auditing he verbally informed his decision to the Vice-Chancellor and the Vice-Chancellor consented to it. The Vice-Chancellor also consented to pay the auditors' fees for auditing firm Taka 82,000.00 which was forwarded to the Vice-Chancellor by Prof. Anwarullah Chowdhury at the and of his tenure as Chairman of 'Cha' Unit. The account left by him available in the office was audited and the auditors submitted report year-wise and the last report was submitted on 6-12-93 with the bills for Taka 27,500.00 to the petitioner which was submitted to the Vice-Chancellor along with the audit report and the Vice Chancellor in his turn forwarded the bill with his signature thereon to the Director of Accounts on 26-1-93. On 27-12-93 the daily Ajker Kagaj published a news under the heading "Corruption of Teacher of Dhaka University. Admission fee of Students are not deposited in the Fund". The Bengali version is as follows ; “ছাত্র ভর্তি পরীক্ষা থেকে প্রাপ্ত অর্থ তহবীলে জমা হয় না।”

On the following day a meeting of the Deans of the Faculties was held in the office of the Vice-Chancellor to consider publication of the aforesaid news item. The Vice-Chancellor in the meeting stated that he gave his consent to the petitioner to have the accounts of the fund of 'gha' unit audited by Chartered Accountant and he also stated that he received the audit report. Thereafter the Chairman and Members of the Admission Committee of the said Unit for the year 1992-93 sent a letter to the Vice-Chancellor and Chairman of the Syndicate of the University on 1-1-94 condemning the action of the petitioner for having the fund audited and demanding his punishment and demanding rejection of the illegal audit report and demanding apology from the petitioner to Prof. Chowdhury and other members of the Admission Committee for the year 1992-93. The letter was placed in the meeting of the Syndicate held on 1-1-94 and the Syndicate adopted resolution to the effect that the audit of the fund as published in the newspaper has neither been done appropriately nor following legal procedure and, as such, according to the members present in the meeting it was not acceptable to the Syndicate and was not operative. It also expressed its indignation for the action taken by the Dean of the Faculty of Social Science in auditing the fund and termed the same was motivated and condemnable. It was resolved in the meeting that the Syndicate would take step in respect of irregularity in the admission matters and other matters on the basis of the report if received. The petitioner wrote letter on 4-1-94 to the Vice-Chancellor and in his turn the Vice-Chancellor replied to the same on 17-1-94. Again on 6-1-94 the petitioner wrote another letter to the Vice-Chancellor requesting him to inform who were the members present in the meeting of the Syndicate held on 1-1-94. Accordingly, the Registrar of the University on 16-1-94 informed that there were 14 members present including Prof. Anwarullah Chowdhury. Although such resolution was taken in the meeting of the Syndicate, no copy of the resolution was forwarded to the petitioner who was condemned in the said meeting. As a result the petitioner complained to the Vice-Chancellor about the non-receipt of such resolution. Thereafter, the copy of the resolution of the Syndicate was forwarded to the petitioner by the Registrar of the University on 5-2-94 (Annexure-G).

It reads in the following terms:"

“নং-৬০৬৭৭৭

রেজিষ্ট্রারের অফিস,

ঢাকা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়,

ঢাকা-১০০০।

তারিখ-৫/২/১৯৯৪ ইং।

উক্ত এ, এক, মনোয়ার উদ্দীন আহম্মদ,

ডীন, সামাজিক বিজ্ঞান অনুষদ,

ঢাকা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়, ঢাকা-১০০০।

প্রিয় মহোদয়,

আপনাকে আদিষ্ট হইয়া জানাইতেছি যে, বিশ্ববিদ্যালায়ের ১ম বর্ষ সম্মান ‘ঘ’ ইউনিটের ভর্তির ফরম বিক্রয়ের অর্থসম্পর্কে সিন্ডিকেট (১-১-৯৪) কর্তৃক নিম্নোক্ত সিদ্ধান্ত গৃহীত হইয়াছে উঃ-

“বিশ্ব বিদ্যালয়ের প্রথম বর্ষ সম্মানের ’ঘ' ইউনিটের ভর্তির ফরম বিক্রয়লব্ধ অর্থের অডিট সম্পর্কে সংবাদপত্রে প্রকাশিত খবরের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে জনসংযোগ অফিসারের ২৭-১২-১৩ ইং তারিখের প্রতিবাদ এবং ১৯৯২-৯৩ শিক্ষাবর্ষের 'ঘ' ইউনিট ভর্তি কমিটির সদস্যদের দরখাস্ত সভায় বিবেচনা করা হয় এবং বিষয়টির উপর বিস্তারিত আলোচনা করা হয়। সিন্ডিকেটেব্র এ সভা মনে করে যে, গত ১০ বৎসর যাবৎ ১ম বর্ষ সমান শ্রেণীতে ভর্তির দায়িত্ব বিভিন্ন অনুষদের ডীনগণ অত্যন্ত দক্ষতা, নিষ্ঠা ও সততার সাথে পালন করে আসছেন এবং এ ভর্তি প্রক্রিয়া তাই জনগণের আস্তা লাভ করেছে৷

এমতাবস্থায়-

(ক) দৈনিক আজকের কাগজের ২৭শে ডিসেম্বর, ১৯৯৩ সংখ্যায় ১১৯২-৯৩ শিক্ষা বর্ষের 'ঘ' ইউনিটের ১ম বর্ষ স্নাতক সম্মান শ্রেণীতে ভর্তি আয়-ব্যায় অডিট করা সম্পর্কে যে খবর প্রকাশিত হয়েছে তা বিশ্বৰিদ্যালয়ের যথাযথ কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক করা হয়নি কিংবা তা বৈধ্ প্রক্রিয়া অনুসরন পুর্বক হয়নি বলে সিন্ডিকেটের নিকট উক্ত অডিট রিপোর্ট গ্রহণযোগ্য নয় এবং সংগত কারনেই উহা অকার্যকর। স্বতঃ প্রবৃত হয়ে সামাজিক বিজ্ঞান অনুষযের বর্তমান ডীনের এ ধরনের অডিট করার ঘটনা ডিন্ডিকেট উদ্দেশ্যমুলক ও নিন্দনীয় বলে মনে করে।

(খ) ভর্তির সংক্রান্ত কিংবা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে অন্য কোন ধরনের অনিয়ম-এর সুনির্দিষ্ট অভিযোগ আসলে সে ব্যাপারে সিন্ডিকেট প্রয়োজনীয় পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করবে।

আপনার বিশ্বস্ত

স্বাঃ/আ,জ,শিকদার, রেজিষ্টার,

ঢাকা বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়।”

3. This Rule is resisted by filing affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the respondents. The deponent states that he is competent to swear the affidavit as authorised under Dhaka University Order, 1973, Statute, Ordinances, Rules and Regulations framed thereunder. He further states that he is authorised by the respondents to answer the allegations. The respondents are the University of Dhaka and the Vice-Chancellor and Chairman of the Syndicate. In the affidavit-in reply to the statements made in paras 1-3 of the writ petition he merely says that these are matters of record and no comment is necessary from him. In respect of statement made in para-4 of the petition he states the Prof. Anwarullah Chowdhury was elected Dean of the Faculty of Social Science not in July, 1989 but in September, 1989 and was again re-elected Dean of the said Faculty in 1991 and he denied the correctness of the statements made in the said paragraph of the petition so far as it relates to the first sentence. He admits that the petitioner succeeded the earlier Dean and worked as Chairman of the 'gha' Unit of the Admission Committee. He commented that question of left over business is wholly unwarranted and irrelevant inasmuch as the same is nothing but a routine work assigned by the Vice-Chancellor to the Dean. In reply to statements made in para-5 of the petition he states that the duty of the petitioner as Chairman and in charge of 'Gha' unit Admission Committee was to hold and supervise the admission tests and examinations for admission of the year 1993-94 and he has nothing to do in the matter of holding examination and incidental thereto of the previous years nor authorised to look into the conduct of the previous Chairman. He says that those are functions of the Vice-Chancellor. In getting the fund audited he proceeds to say that the petitioner exceeded his authority and jurisdiction by appointing a private auditor for the alleged purpose and the statement that he received verbal consent of the Vice-Chancellor to hold audit of the previous year was not true and the same was fabricated and created statement. He says that the Dean is not the authority of the University and no request was made to Prof. Anwarullah Chowdhury, the previous Chairman, to hand over papers as alleged in the petition. Regarding the audit his reply was that it was irrelevant and the bill submitted by the Chartered Accountant in a routine manner was marked by the Vice-Chancellor for scrutiny and necessary action by the Director of Accounts of the Dhaka University. The noting of the Vice-Chancellor on the bill itself cannot be construed to be an acceptance of the audit report and for a direction to pay off the bill. It is further replied that in absence of any provision for appointing a private auditor neither the audit report can be accepted nor the bill can be accepted nor the bill can be paid. The deponent further states that news as published in the Daily' Ajker Kagaj' has tarnished the image of the Chairman of the 'Gha' unit and it also constitutes an act of imputation and lowering down the authority and dignity of the Dhaka University. He further states with emphasis that publication of the news was motivated and it hampered the reputation and prestige of Prof. Anwarullah Chowdhury, Ex-Chairman of the Admission Committee of 'Gha' Unit including the whole nation and others and the demand made pursuant to the resolution passed in the meeting held on 1-1-94 is just action. As the Syndicate did not find any legal basis for such auditing the accounts, it was not acceptable to it and the petitioner himself took the responsibility of having the accounts audited by a private auditor and caused publication of the same in the newspaper for collateral purpose with malafide motive. In reply to statement made in para-11 of the petition he simply says that it was communicated to the petitioner who attended the meeting of the Syndicate and no bar was in law to hold such meeting. In reply to statement made in para-12 of the petition he reiterates what he said in the earlier paragraphs of the affidavit.

4. The petitioner further filed supplementary affidavit wherein it is stated that the Senate in a meeting held on 23-25th June, 1993 discussed the matter of the fund and audit of the accounts and it resolved as appears at page 320 of the Proceedings published under the authority of the University (Annexure-I to the supplementary affidavit) It says amongst others:

“ভর্তি সংক্রান্ত অর্থকরী কেন্দ্রিয়ভাবে নিয়ন্ত্রণ এবং অডিট করানোর বিষয়ঃ

(২) ভর্তি পরীক্ষা বিভাগ এবং ডীনের কার্য্যালয় থেকে গ্রহণ করা হোক যা বর্তমানে চালু রয়েছে। কিন্তু অর্থকরী বিষয়টি কেন্দ্রীয় ভাবে নিয়ন্ত্রণ করা এবং বহিস্থ অডিট দ্বারা অডিট করা বাঞ্চনীয় বলে-এ সভা মনে করে।”

It is stated in the supplementary affidavit by the petitioner that he took over charge as Dean on 31-7-93 and caused the audit of the fund collected during 1989-90, 1990-91, 1991-92 and 1992-93 and accordingly he submitted the audit report.

5. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the petitioner, first contends that the censure in the form of condemnation is minor penalty under para 13 (1) of Chapter-XVI-A of the Dhaka University Ordinance and Regulations (as amended up to June 1986) and such penalty pursuant to the resolution of the Syndicate in violation of Paragraph 45(3) and (4) of the First Statutes of the Dhaka University Order 1973 (President's Order No.11 of 1973) is without lawful authority. Secondly, the resolution of the Syndicate is violative of the principle of natural justice inasmuch as before passing such resolution in censuring the petitioner he was not given any chance of hearing. His next contention is that it is not the University which has authority to deal with the funds created out of collection of the admission fees of the intending students seeking admission to the 1st year Honours Classes but it is the Dean and the Chairman of the Admission Committee so formed or constituted by the Vice-Chancellor. So saying he submits that the Syndicate had no authority to hold the meeting and to pass resolution condemning and censuring the petitioner' Khondker further submits that the resolution of the Syndicate in condemning by censure the petitioner is in malafide and it was for collateral purposes, and, as such, the action impugned is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

6. Mr. Zakir Ahmed, learned Advocate for the respondents, made an attempt to urge, that mere forwarding the Bill and the audit report to the Director of Accounts signed by the Vice-Chancellor cannot be said that he had given his consent to the, petitioner for getting the account audited and accepted such bill. This contention is devoid of any sense as nowhere in the four corners of the affidavit in-opposition there is any statement that the Vice-Chancellor has denied giving his consent to have the account audited and the report together with the Bill accepted- In this case as once the Vice-Chancellor had accorded permission for auditing and after having received the audit report and the Bill sent the same after signing to the Director of Accounts and there being no denial from the Vice-Chancellor, the contention of Mr. Zakir Ahmed has no leg to stand and, we cannot but hold that the, audit was done, in due course having sanction of the Vice-Chancellor.

7. Now the question is whether the Syndicate acted within its authority empowered by First Statute of the Dhaka University Order, 1973 (President's Order 11 of 1973) read with: paragraph No 13 of Chapter-XVI of the Ordinance and Regulations of the Dhaka University.

Paragraph No. 45(3) and (4) read:

"45(3). No teacher or officer shall be penalised or dismissed except on the ground of moral turpitude or inefficiency or conduct prejudicial to, service, discipline or unbecoming of University employee and no action shall be taken on such ground without an enquiry by an Inquiry Committee to be set up by the Syndicate in which opportunity shall be provided to the teacher and officer concerned to represent his case."

(4). If a prima facie case is established against the employee concerned as a result of inquiry, a Tribunal consisting of one representative of the nominee of the employee concerned shall be set up by the Syndicate with one of them as convener to consider the case and recommend to the Syndicate, of such action as it deems fit"

<u>8. A careful examination of sub clauses; (3) and (4) of Paragraph 45 manifestly makes it clear that for imposition of a penalty upon a teacher an Inquiry Committee is to be set up by the Syndicate to enquire into the allegations and the Inquiry Committee so set up after holding inquiry, if finds that a prima facie case is established against employee concerned, the Syndicate is to set up a Tribunal on the report of the Inquiry Committee to consider the case and, to recommend to the Syndicate such action as it deems fit. Therefore, it seems that for the purpose of inflicting any punishment. Upon, a teacher of the, University first an Inquiry Committee is to be established by the Syndicate to, enquire into the allegations and on submission of the recommendation of the Inquiry Committee after holding inquiry giving an opportunity to thee teacher to be heard concerned with its recommendation to Syndicate, the Syndicate is to take action against the teacher.</u>

<u>9. But in the instant case the Syndicate of its own motion censured the petitioner without complying with the requirements of sub clauses (3) and (4) of Paragraph No. 45 of the First Schedule Dhaka University Ordinance and Regulations, 1973.</u>

<u>Chapter XVI-A of  Dhaka University Ordinance and Regulations is on Enquiry Committee and Tribunal; for Teacher& and Officers. This Chapter reads:</u>

<u>"CHAPTER XVI-A</u>

<u>Enquiry Committee and Tribunal (Teachers and Officers) Regulations, 1980.</u>

<u>…………………</u>

<u>13(1)(a) Censure.</u>

<u>The resolution of the Syndicate to the effect “স্বতঃ প্রবৃত হয়ে সামাজিক বিজ্ঞান ���নুষদের বর্তমান ডিনের এ ধরনের অডিট করার ঘটনা সিন্ডিকেট উদ্দেশ্য মূলক ও নিন্দনীয় বলে মনে করে।” is an expression of condemnation and "censure" within the meaning of paragraph 13(1)(a) of Chapter XVI-A of the Ordinance and Regulations. It is consistently held by the superior Courts of the Sub-continent that the censure, in respect of an incumbent either of the Government or of a local Body, like the University before us, is a punishment and before inflicting a punishment the person so punished shall be given a hearing or a chance to confront the allegations made against him. This is not done here.</u>

<u>A reference to the supplementary affidavit also convinced us that for the uniform practice and more so in view of the afore-quoted portion of the resolution in Bengali version the petitioner is not at all subject to such censure as has been done by the Syndicate in the meeting held as noted earlier and accordingly, it seems to us that the resolution was taken malafide and for collateral purposes.</u>

<u>10. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the resolution has been passed by the Syndicate without any lawful authority and is also violative of the principle of natural justice.</u>

In the result, the Rule is made absolute with a cost of Taka 1000.00 (Taka one thousand only).

End.

case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated March 30, 1997 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Order No. 1383 of 1997)
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: The appeal by leave is against the judgment and order dated March 30, 1997 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division passed in Civil Order No. 1383 of 1997 rejecting the revisional application summarily. The revisional application was filed against the order dated 19-2-1997 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore allowing an application filed under Order 1, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereupon striking out the name of defendant Nos. 3 and 4 (herein respondent Nos. 1 and 2)

2. Facts, in short, are that appellant Bank has filed suit, Money Suit No. 7 of 1996, in the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Jessore for realisation of Taka 39,32,725.92 (as on 24-6-1996) impleading as many as 7 defendants including the present respondent Nos. 1 and 2 stating, inter alia, that on the prayer of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 the Bank by its sanction letter dated 16-7-1995 allowed loan of Taka 5,00,000 by way of Cash Credit (hypothecation) and Taka 30,00,000 by way of Cash Credit (pledge) and the loanees executed charge-documents in favour of the Bank, that proprietors (defendant Nos. 3 and 4) of Messrs Chowdhury Trading, a dealer of the defendant No. 7 (Zia Fertiliser Company Limited) got allotment of 1,000 metric tons of Urea fertiliser from the said defendant but due to paucity of fund they were not in a position to withdraw the said fertiliser and in that situation they entered into an agreement with the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 for sale of the said fertiliser and made an advance sale of fertiliser upon concluding written agreement for sale, that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on the basis of said agreement for sale obtained a demand draft in favour of defendant No. 7 for the price of the fertiliser from the Bank as against the loan sanctioned in the name of said defendants, that while the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 obtained demand draft from the Bank, the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 executed a receipt acknowledging receipt of said demand draft as well as promised to deliver the letter of allotment to the Bank and also undertook to give necessary letter of authority in favour of the designated person of the Bank so that the said agent of the Bank can lift the fertiliser from the defendant No. 7 ( Zia Fertiliser Company Ltd.), that in due course the demand draft obtained from the Bank was deposited in the office of the fertiliser factory. It may be mentioned that the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 made over to the Bank letter of allotmentissued by the fertiliser factory, the receipt granted by defendant No. 7 acknowledging receiving of the Bank draft and the letter of authorisation executed in favour of Bank's nominee authorising lifting of fertiliser allotted to defendant Nos. 3 and 4.

3. It is the case of the Bank that allotted consignment of fertiliser was not delivered to the authorised officer of the Bank by the fertiliser factory and that the Bank could not realise the amount of the Bank draft.

4. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 (defendant Nos. 3 and 4) entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint.

5. Thereafter, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application under Order 1, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for striking out their names from the plaint on the ground that they were neither the borrowers of the Bank nor they are the guarantors in respect of the amount which was sanctioned as loan in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2.

6. The Court of Subordinate Judge upon hearing the parties allowed the application filed under Order I, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2. Thereupon, the appellant moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division summarily rejected the revisional application.

7. Leave was granted to consider, the submissions that liability of the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 for the loan in question has been clearly made out in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the plaint, but the High Court Division as well as the court below upon a total non-consideration of the facts of the case and the law on the subject illegally caused the names of the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 to be struck out from the plaint, that defendant Nos. 3 and 4 having admitted, undertaken and declared their liability to the Bank the High Court Division was wrong in upholding the finding of the trial Court to the effect that plaintiff will get no decree against them as they were not borrowers and that their presence will serve no purpose, inasmuch as the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 nowhere provides that the suit may only be filed in the Artha Rin Adalat against the borrower, and further that the Court could not at this stage give any finding or speculate about the decree that may be passed, that section 5(1) of the Ain provides that all suits concerning realisation of loans of a Bank will be filed in the Artha Rin Adalat, that there is no provision that such a suit may only be filed against a borrower/guarantor, that High Court Division was in error in upholding the order of the Artha Rin Adalat inasmuch as the suit being for realisation of a loan which is within the definition of loan as given in section 2(kha) of the said Ain inasmuch as there are documents signed by the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 showing their liability for it and therefore the finding that the suit will serve no purpose as against those defendants is erroneous in law, that the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 having received and utilised the loan granted by the Bank, which is well within the definition of loan as in section 2(kha), the High Court Division is wrong in upholding the order of striking out the names of the said defendants who were necessary and property parties in the suit.

8. It is seen from the plaint that the Bank sanctioned loan of Taka 5,00,000 by way of Cash-Credit (hypothecation) and Taka 30,00,000 by way of Cash-Credit (pledge) in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. As it appears the defendant Nos.1 and 2 got sanction of the aforesaid loan to lift 1,000 metric tons of fertiliser from the Zia fertiliser factory which they purchased in advance from defendant Nos. 3 and 4, who got allotment of 1,000 metric tons of fertiliser, to be lifted from Zia fertiliser factory. The said defendants made advance sale of the fertiliser to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and in that regard the said defendants and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 entered into an agreement representing the sale of the fertiliser. The Bank on the representation of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 made upon presenting agreement of sale entered into between the said defendants and defendant Nos. 3 and 4 issued a Demand Draft in favour of the defendant No. 7, Zia Fertiliser Factory. It may be mentioned the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 being the allottee acknowledged the receipt of the Demand Draft and gave an undertaking to deposit in the Bank letter of allotment and other connected papers. It appears that the said papers were deposited with the Bank along with a letter of authorisation in favour of authorised officer of the Bank authorising him to withdraw 1,000 metric tons fertilisers from the Zia fertiliser factory. It is apparent from the papers on the record that since defendant Nos. 3 and 4 made advance sale of 1,000 metric tons of fertiliser to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, they obtained loan from the Bank upon hypothecation/pledge of the said fertiliser and the Bank facilitated the said defendants to utilise the loan money on the basis of their agreement of purchase with defendant Nos. 3 and 4.

9. It appears from the pleading of the plaintiff that ultimately, the Bank could not take delivery of the fertiliser from the Zia Fertiliser Factory and also did not get the amount of the Demand Draft and, in that state of the matter, Bank filed the suit impleading as many as 7 persons as defendants. It is seen from the materials on record that defendant Nos. 3 and 4 having had allotment of 1,000 metric tons of fertiliser from the Zia fertiliser factory (defendant No.7), they made advance sale of the said fertiliser to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by an agreement of sale. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 upon presenting to the Bank the aforesaid agreement of purchase got the Demand Draft issued in favour of the defendant No. 7 as against the loan sanctioned in their favour in respect of the price of 1,000 metric tons of fertiliser. It also appears from the papers in the record that the Demand Draft issued by the Bank was in favour of the fertiliser factory and the said Demand Draft was deposited in the office of the Zia Fertiliser Company Ltd.

10. The Bank in its plaint has stated that as the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 were unable to lift the fertiliser, which they got allotted in their favour, because of paucity of fund they sold in advance the said fertiliser to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 upon entering into an agreement. It is also the case of the Bank that after entering into the agreement the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as well as defendant Nos. 3 and 4 appeared before the Bank and on the application of defendant Nos.1 and 2 a Demand Draft of Taka 37, 25,000 was issued in favour of the defendant No. 7. It is seen from the averments made in the plaint that the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 for enabling the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as well as the Bank to lift the fertiliser from the defendant No. 7 executed the necessary papers and pursuant thereto the Bank approached the defendant No. 7 for getting delivery of 1,000 metric tons of fertiliser but the defendant No. 7 did not deliver the fertiliser. From the papers on record it is seen that defendant Nos. 3 and 4 after having had made advance sale of the fertiliser, whereof they got allotment from respondent No. 7, to the defendant Nos .1 and 2 upon entering into an agreement the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as loanees of the Bank obtained Demand Draft in favour of the defendant No. 7 towards the price of the fertiliser. It also appears from the papers on record that defendant Nos. 3 and 4 did the necessary things to enable the Bank and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to get delivery of the fertiliser. The admitted position is that Bank advanced loan to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 towards advanced purchase of the fertiliser, allotment whereof was obtained by the defendant Nos. 3 and 4. In the background of the facts and circumstances as transpire from papers on record it appears the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 were not the borrowers, from the Bank and whatever they did, they did so to enable the borrowers of the Bank, i.e. defendant Nos. 1 and 2, being advance purchasers, to get delivery of the fertiliser so sold.

11. The Bank has filed the suit for realisation of the loan amount.

12. In the Artha Rin Adalt Ain, 1990 (the Ain) in section 2(kha) ' ঋণ ' has been defined as: "(১) অগ্রিম,ধার,নগদ ঋণ,ওভার ড্রাফট,ব্যাংকিং ক্রেডিট,বাটাকৃত বা ক্রয়কৃত বিল বা অন্য যে কোনো আর্থিক আনুকূল্য বা সুযোগ-সুবিধা ,যে নামেই অভিহিত হউক না কেন

(২) গ্যারান্টি,ইনডেমনিটি,ঋণপত্র বা অন্য কোনো আর্থিক বন্দোবস্ত , যাহা কোনো আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান ঋণ গ্রহীতার পক্ষে প্রদান বা জারী করে বা দায় হিসাবে গ্রহণ করে "

13. As per provision of the Ain, financial institution, as the appellant, is required to file suit in the Artha Rin Adalat established under the Ain against the person who has/had availed the facility or has facilitated one to avail the facility as in section 2(kha) of the Ain and failed to discharge the obligation within stipulated time as per undertaking given at the time of availing one or more of the species as in section 2(kha) of the Ain. The obligation of repayment of ' ঋণ ' as defined in section 2(kha) of the Ain is of the one who has availed the same from financial institution as well as of the one who either facilitated the one to avail ' ঋণ ' or secured repayment of the ' ঋণ ' and only these categories are to be held responsible in case of default in the repayment of the amount became due as against the ' ঋণ ' availed from financial institution. The provisions of the Ain, and particularly the provision of section 2(kha) of the Ain, do not contemplate that the person to whom loanee(s), in the instant case defendant Nos. 1 and 2, had an obligation and the loanee with the loan amount discharged his obligation to that person and in such situation the person as regard whom loanee discharged his obligation would be considered a loanee or that would be under obligation to discharge loanee's obligation in case of loanee's failure to pay the amount became due against the loanee. The provisions of the Ain also do not contemplate that a loanee who at one time entered into an agreement of advance purchase of certain merchandise and upon presenting such agreement he utilised the amount sanctioned by the financial institution as loan and that the other party to agreement of advance purchase did the concomitant/necessary things for the materialisation of the agreement in such a situation the other party to the agreement would be considered a loanee or that would be under an obligation to discharge the obligation of the person (s) in whose favour the financial institution in fact sanctioned money as loan or ‘ঋণ’.

<u>14. From the averments made in the plaint it is seen that Cash-Credit (hypothecation) and Cash-Credit (pledge) facilities were allowed to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. It also appears from the averments made in the plaint and the papers placed on the record that said loans were given to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to enable them to lift the fertiliser which they have purchased in advance from the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 who got the allotment of the fertiliser from defendant No. 7. In our opinion, upon making advance sale of the fertiliser the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 had hardly anything to do except facilitating the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to lift the fertiliser, which the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 did as regard the fertiliser in question. From the papers on the record it is seen that the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 to make the agreement of advance sale fruitful they did everything to enable the Bank and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to lift the fertiliser from respondent No. 7.</u>

<u>15. In the background of the materials on record and the discussions made hereinbefore, in our view, it cannot be said that defendant Nos. 3 and 4 obtained loan from the Bank or received any financial facilities from the Bank and that they are also not the guarantors in respect of the loan made available by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2.</u>

<u>16. The learned Counsel appearing for the appellant wants us to read in the definition of ' ঋণ ' as given in section 2(kha) of the Artha Rin Adalat that whatever facility or facilities one obtains even though not a loanee out of the loan sanctioned by the Bank such person shall also be considered a loanee of the Bank. This submission as appears to have been made in the background of the fact that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 made advance purchase of the fertiliser in respect whereof defendant Nos. 3 and 4 got a letter of allotment from defendant No. 7 and that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on the basis of the agreement of advance purchase obtained loan from the Bank to lift the fertiliser so advance purchased from the defendant Nos. 3 and 4. It is difficult to read, as the learned Counsel intends, in the definition of the At as in section 2(kha) of the Ain that in the background of particular transaction one of the parties to the transaction obtains loan for materialisation of the transaction to his benefit or to discharge his obligation to the other party arising out of said transaction, the party as regard whom the loanee has discharged his obligation, such party would also be considered a loanee of the Bank being the beneficiary. The definition of the ‘ঋণ’ as given in the Ain cannot be stretched in the manner as the learned Counsel wants us to stretch since the Bank, as in the instant case, did not sanction and allow any loan to the defendant Nos. 3 and 4, rather the Bank sanctioned loan to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and allowed said defendants to avail the loan granted and, as such, it is the liability to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to pay back the dues against the loan.</u>

<u>17. It is a hard proposition as because the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in utilisation of the loan placed before the Bank the agreement entered into on one part between defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and the other part between defendant Nos. 3 and 4 making advance sale of fertiliser allotment whereof defendant Nos. 3 and 4 got from defendant No. 7 and, as such, defendant Nos. 3 and 4 are also the loanees of the Bank.</u>

<u>18. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view the High Court Division has committed no error in refusing to interfere with the order of the trial Court striking out the names of the defendant Nos. 3 and 4.</u>

19. The learned Counsel for the appellant upon referring to the provision of Order rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure submitted that in the background of the facts of the case impleading of the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 was quite legal and that High Court Division erred in refusing to interfere with the order of the trial Court striking out the names of the defendants. In support of the aforesaid submission, the learned Counsel has referred to the case of Bangladesh Railway vs Messrs Sinaf Racht Chartering and Ship Breaking Corporation reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 115. Suffice it to say the facts of the reported case are quite distinct from the facts of the instant case. The provision of Order I rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure contemplates a situation where several persons may be impleaded in the suit as defendants if relief so sought for has arisen against them out of the same act or transaction or series of acts or transactions. From the materials on record it is seen that defendant Nos. 3 and 4 were not parties to the transaction i.e. sanctioning of loan by the Bank to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, and also availing of loan facility allowed by the Bank. The Bank on the application of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 allowed loan to enable them to lift the fertiliser which they purchased from the defendant Nos. 3 and 4. An agreement was entered into between the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 as regard sale of the fertiliser and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by placing the said agreement for sale, as it appears, obtained loan and utilised the same for lifting the fertiliser from the defendant No. 7. In the background of the said fact, it cannot be said that the loan as the Bank granted to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and utilised by them and the transaction that took place between the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and defendant Nos. 3 and 4 is same or one. As such, upon resorting to the provision of Order I, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure it cannot be said that Bank has quite legally filed the suit impleading the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 as the defendants along with others.

Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed. There is no order as to costs.

End.

TH Khan with Amir Hossain Chowdhury and Rezina Chowdhury, Advocates - For the Petitioner. 
Md Rafiqul Islam with Md SR Khoshnabish, Advocates - For the Opposite Parties.
